01 — About

A life measured in service, not in campaigns.

I come from a political clan of Victorias City — a descendant of Alejandro Acuña Yap Quiña, a philanthropist of Chinese ancestry who donated his landholdings to the then Municipality of Victorias, the ground on which the city now stands.

My family came from a simple household. My parents were employees, and what they bequeathed to us was not wealth but education. Father always talked politics around the dinner table; Mother always made sure the table was full. That childhood, I am convinced, is why public service never felt like a career to me — it felt like an inheritance.

At sixteen, in 1992, I was elected Sangguniang Kabataan Chairman of my village and eventually Federation President of the Municipality of Victorias — becoming an ex-officio member of the Town Council while serving as Provincial Federation Vice President. A second term later took me to the Provincial Board, and to the National Executive Board of the SK National Federation, where I helped draft the present SK Constitution and By-Laws.

“Give a man a fish, and you feed him for a day; teach a man to fish, and you feed him for a lifetime.”

— the principle behind the LGU–TESDA skills training partnership

In between, I studied Community Development Economics at the University of St. La Salle–Bacolod, later completed a Bachelor of Science in Nursing, and returned to Negros as Chief of Staff to the Mayor and then City Administrator of Victorias City. Today I sit once more in the City Council — but the through-line never changed: pariente sang masa.

02 — The Record

Four decades in public life.

  1. 1992

    Age 16 — SK Chairman, Barangay V

    Elected Sangguniang Kabataan Chairman of his village; soon Federation President of the Municipality of Victorias and ex-officio member of the Town Council.

  2. 1996

    SK President, Negros Occidental

    Re-elected from the barangay to the municipal and provincial level. Ex-officio member of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, and National Assistant Auditor of the SK National Federation.

  3. 1998

    Cityhood — R.A. No. 8488

    As SK Federation President he personally delivered to the Senate the SK resolution supporting Victorias' cityhood. The law was signed by President Fidel V. Ramos on February 11, 1998 and ratified on March 21, 1998 — now Charter Day.

  4. 2002

    End of the youth chapter

    Two decades of Sangguniang Barangay, Sangguniang Bayan and Sangguniang Panlalawigan service. Most of the infrastructure and ordinances built in city and province — including the cityhoods of Sipalay and Himamaylan — carry his votes.

  5. 2014

    Chief of Staff to the Mayor

    Six years inside city government, translating policy into programmes on the ground.

  6. 2020

    City Administrator, Victorias City

    Appointed Administrator of the City of Victorias — the first former youth councillor to hold the post.

  7. 2022

    Elected to the City Council

    Returns to the chamber as Councilor of Victorias City, 3rd Congressional District, Negros Occidental.

  8. 2024

    City Ordinance No. 2024-159

    Authors the “Grow-a-Forest Project of Victorias City” — the Adopt-a-Forest Program. Approved by the Sangguniang Panlungsod on November 18, 2024 and signed by Mayor Javier Miguel L. Benitez on January 13, 2025.

  9. 2025

    “Together for the Trees”

    Launches the first planting under the ordinance during the 27th Kadalag-an Festival and the International Day of Forests, with 2,500 endemic seedlings planted and 10,100 more donated by PEMO and PENRO.

03 — Programs

Legislation that touches ground.

Ordinance No. 2024-159

Adopt-a-Forest Program

The flagship ordinance of his council career makes forest stewardship a shared civic duty. Government agencies, private organisations, schools, barangays and ordinary citizens are invited to adopt one hectare — either in the northwestern part of Mt. Silay in Gawahon, within the Northern Negros Natural Park, or in open public spaces designated by the Victorias City Environment and Natural Resources Office.

Upland
2,500 native tree seedlings
Coastal
5,000 malihaw seedlings
Care period
3 years of watering, grooming & protection
Oversight
Tripartite agreement + monitoring committee

The City Government supplies seedlings and handles transport and site preparation; sponsors cover maintenance; residents of Gawahon are employed to keep the trees alive. Barangay XI was the first to adopt an area, setting the example for others.

Botika Sang Masa

Bringing the city government's health programme down to the purok — medicines, vitamins and hygiene supplies distributed directly to barangay folk, in faithful compliance with the Anti-Epal Policy.

Adopt a Victoriasanon Family

Five consecutive years, since 2021, of showing up for one family each September — a fisherfolk household in 2026 — with the CSWD, because a simple act of kindness still brings hope.

Skills & livelihood

Backing the LGU–TESDA partnership so women and communities gain durable skills and sustainable livelihood — self-sufficiency instead of one-off assistance.

The sugar industry

Long advocacy for the sugar bill that would protect the livelihood of sugar-producing provinces — Negros Occidental chief among them — from a subsector too often left out of the room.

Charter Day

Severo A. Palanca, father of the cityhood

The town leader whose tireless lobbying turned Victorias into a component city. Congressman Kako Lacson, Senators Pimentel, Sotto, Maceda, and President Fidel V. Ramos were among the allies — and a 7-year-old boy carrying an SK resolution to the Senate.

Tribute

Lola Aling — Rosalina J. Hautea

Teacher for 38 years, retired in 1988, and the woman who raised him from the age of seven. “Imo lawas imo kulo, imo kalag imo bakiro” — you manage your own body, you manage your own soul. He was her adopted son, and says so still.

Idiong Bantug
